title: Development of a Multivariable Proxy Model for Six-Minute Walk Distance (6MWD) in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) Using Machine Learning Methods (682)
contribution: A 6MWD proxy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy from routinely available variables: optimal regression trees fit best under ten-fold CV (CV-R² 0.85 against 0.83 for random forests), with a cross-validated linear model close behind (0.79), on 59 placebo-arm patients (abstract).

quotes.text: Predictors were selected using regression trees, optimal regression trees (ORT), random forests, and LASSO regression.

contribution: Learned hashing for streaming frequency estimation: an optimization formulation on an observed prefix (solved exactly or approximately) plus a learned hash for unseen elements, with one to two orders of magnitude lower average error than existing approaches (abstract); extended abstract of S366.
problem_entry: {IO+ML} Streaming frequency estimation under limited storage; state-of-the-art sketches rely on random hashing (abstract).

assumptions: An observed stream prefix is available; limited storage; synthetic data and real search-query data (abstract).
proof_devices: Optimization formulation solved exactly and approximately (abstract); details in S366 (card s14)
experiments: Synthetic and real-world search-query data; one to two orders of magnitude lower average per-element estimation error and 45–90% lower expected magnitude of error (abstract).
positioning: Against state-of-the-art streaming frequency estimation algorithms that rely on random hashing (abstract); the full paper is S366 (TKDE, same authors and title; card s14) [inferred from titles].
writing: Contrast-first: the second sentence sets the approach against random hashing; gains quantified in orders of magnitude (abstract).
limits_future: Not stated in the extended abstract.

method_links.note: A component another tradition randomizes (hashing) is rewritten as an optimization problem; Taste mark 3.
Randomized, not greedy, step replaced; exact or approximate solves with no certificate, limit or solver stated; incumbent duel given only as aggregate error ratios.

transferable: Replace a randomized component by one optimized on an observed sample, and train a model to extend the optimized assignment to unseen items (abstract).

quotes.text: Contrary to state-of-the-art streaming frequency estimation algorithms, which heavily rely on random hashing to maintain the frequency distribution of the data steam using limited storage, the proposed approach exploits an observed stream prefix to near-optimally hash elements and compress the target frequency distribution.

We develop and solve (exactly and approximately) an optimization formulation, which enables us to compute optimal or near-optimal hashing schemes for elements seen in the observed stream prefix; then, we use machine learning to hash unseen elements.

assumptions: MSKCC patients with resected primary non-metastatic GIST (1982–2017), intermediate or high risk by Miettinen criteria, complete follow-up (117 of 1,007); predictors mitotic count, size and site; external Polish (363) and Spanish (239) cohorts (abstract). Identification of treatment effects from observational data is not discussed in the abstract.
proof_devices: Counterfactual random forest read by an optimal policy tree trained on its counterfactual predictions (abstract)
experiments: OPT cut-offs: sensitivity 92.7% and specificity 33.9% internally; externally sensitivity 95.4% (Spain) and 92.4% (Poland); 29% and 35% spared; 33 durations tested, 5 years best (abstract).
positioning: Against current guidelines for adjuvant imatinib (abstract); uses Optimal Policy Trees (H005, by Amram, Dunn and Zhuo).
writing: Lancet structured abstract; strong claim that the 5-year finding could be the best evidence until the 2028 trial reports (abstract).
limits_future: Observational, small internal cohort (117), low specificity (33.9%); a randomized trial expected in 2028 (abstract).

method_links.note: Decision (treatment and duration) is the object, checked against guidelines and on external cohorts, with the pending RCT named as what the evaluation cannot replace.

assumptions: Unit commitment under load and capacity uncertainty in an ARO setting (abstract); the preprint S531 uses linear decision rules with binaries fixed (card s19).

Prices read off the dual of the LDR robust counterpart with binaries fixed, in the preprint S531 (card s19)

title: Skip Transformers: Efficient Inference through Skip-Routing

problem_entry: {ML} Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (IA3, LoRA) reduces training but not inference cost (abstract).
key_idea: Skip-routing: routers after each self-attention block send each token through the FFN or skip it (abstract).
assumptions: Fine-tuning of pretrained Transformers; new penalty terms in the loss and a specific router weight initialization (abstract).
experiments: Downstream tasks during fine-tuning; specifics not in the abstract.
positioning: Builds on sparse mixture-of-experts and conditional computation; contrasts with IA3 and LoRA (abstract).
writing: Explicit hedge: results 'although preliminary' (abstract).
limits_future: Preliminary results; motivates sparsely activated Transformers as a direction (abstract).
coauthors: M. Peroni (works.json)

quotes.text: We refer to this process as skip-routing.

title: When is More Better? Efficient and Adaptive Modality Acquisition in Multimodal Learning
contribution: Efficient Adaptive Modality Acquisition: multi-stage, cost-aware selection of which modalities to acquire, via a learned compositional value function over subsets optimized by submodular optimization, scaling linearly in the number of modalities (README text of the abstract).

title: Identifying subsets of patients with retroperitoneal sarcoma who benefit from radiotherapy: an Interpretable AI reanalysis of the STRASS randomised trial
contribution: Reanalysis of the STRASS trial: a random survival forest read by an optimal policy tree finds two subgroups (younger well-differentiated and curatively operated dedifferentiated liposarcoma) with significant radiotherapy benefit, while the STRASS and STREXIT subgroup rules show none within STRASS (abstract).
problem_entry: {DA+ML+AP} STRASS showed no overall radiotherapy benefit, and its subgroup readings conflict; identify and quantify who benefits (abstract).
key_idea: Counterfactual random survival forest on randomized data, partitioned by an optimal policy tree on predicted benefit, then compared with the trial's own subgroup rules (abstract).
assumptions: All 266 randomized STRASS patients; pretreatment variables; 5-year abdominal recurrence-free survival as target (abstract).
proof_devices: Random survival forest read by an optimal policy tree; Kaplan–Meier, Fine–Gray competing risks, IPCW-adjusted estimates and a Cox interaction test (abstract)
experiments: Seven OPT subgroups; combined benefiting subgroups: 3-year ARFS 79% vs 58%, HR 0.40 (p=0.0016); cumulative incidence of abdominal recurrence 17% vs 33%; radiotherapy–age interaction p=0.012 (abstract).
positioning: Against the STRASS subgroup and STREXIT interpretations, which showed no significant improvement when re-evaluated (abstract).
writing: Lancet structured abstract; hedged ('appears to meaningfully improve'); ends by calling for focused future trials (abstract).
limits_future: Post hoc reanalysis of one trial of 266 patients; findings to be substantiated by focused trials before becoming standard of care (abstract).

method_links.note: The decision (radiotherapy) is judged against the field's current subgroup rules (STRASS, STREXIT), and the paper names what its evaluation cannot settle.
